newsitem.title: THAILAND: Shinawatra seen posting lower 96 profit.
newsitem.headline: Shinawatra seen posting lower 96 profit.

text.p: Thai telecom conglomorate, Shinawatra Computer and Communication Plc, is expected to post lower profit in 1996 than last year due to a lack of capital gains and slower growth of its new mobile phone subscribers, analysts said on Friday.
"We expect Shinawatra Computer's net profit this year to be lower than last year," said an analyst at Seamico Securites.
"The company recorded a lot of capital gains from the sale of shares in its units last year. This year the company has not yet made any share sales," he said.
Shinawatra Computer reported a net profit of 3.3 billion baht in 1995 compared with 2.77 billion baht the previous year.
In the first six months of 1996, the company reported a net profit of 1.46 billion baht against 1.92 billion baht the same period last year.
The expected fall in Shinawatra Computer's profit was also attributed to the slow rate of new mobile phone subscribers of its unit, Advanced Info Services Plc, analysts said.
Advanced Info contributed about half of Shinawatra Computer's profit in 1995, they added.
Advanced Info earlier this year targeted to attract about 300,000 new mobile phone subscribers in 1996. At the end of 1995, the company's mobile phone subcribers totalled 660,000.
According to Advanced Info, the number of its subscribers was at around 800,000 by the end of September.
"I don't think Advanced Info's total subcribers will reach 900,000 this year. The company's previous target was too optimistic," said one analyst at a foreign brokerage.
Advanced Info posted a net profit of 1.78 billion baht in the first six months compared with 1.24 billion baht the same period last year.
Analysts said Shinawatra Computer's earnings will also be affected by fiercer competition in mobile phone markets which has reduced profit margins.
"The competition in mobile phone markets is intensifying. This brings the price of mobile phone handsets down significantly," another analyst at Ekachart Finance and Securities said.
